text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000328's 99215 rate is elevated in every complexity band and half of those visits are on low-complexity patients, yet the limited returned charts largely support the billed levels.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern is consistent with upcoding: the 99215 share runs roughly two to three times the all-provider rate in every complexity band, including patients with zero conditions, and the sampled low-complexity 99215s are often for simple diagnoses like Z09 follow-ups, R21 rash or J06.9 URI (e.g., C0196955, C0198770). The documentation points the other way: the unsupported rate on the 17 documented 99215s is below the comparison rate, and even a low-complexity claim such as C0197059 (hypertension only) was documented at high MDM. That support is not decisive, because records cover only about 2% of claims, problem flags appear on more than a third of returned notes, and a few notes claim moderate-plus data review with no lab or test on the claim, which weakly suggests templated or inflated notes. A reviewer should first examine the flagged notes (C0196693, C0196753, C0196771; data flags C0198343, C0198384, C0198431) for cloned language and request the EHR audit trail. They should then pull a larger, targeted chart sample of the 0-1 condition 99215s to test whether high MDM is genuinely supported there."}
